correctness.rationale: A complete 91-word length-45 factor set S is extracted from the 274-symbol ninth substitution iterate. Every length-45 factor of the image of each s in S was independently checked to lie in S. The nonerasing substitution and 45-letter source covering argument prove S exhausts all length-45 factors of the infinite word. The triple predicate has span <=44, hence is equivalent to its condition on S. A 13,244-triple exact search and independent direct-position test return precisely the same 55. Standalone verify.py recreates rather than trusts these numbers. The theorem does not infer infinite claims from finite sampling alone.

originality.rationale: The primary 2022 paper (§4.5, Theorem 29 and Open Problem 30) gives only one explicit Tribonacci triple (4,6,7) and explicitly leaves classification of all triples open. It proves general decidability, not the 55 positive triples, 13,189 negative cases, or the 91-factor substitution-closed certificate through the nontrivial sixth substitution scale. Comparison of the actual statements, bounded parameters, and published mathematical records revealed no dominating exact bounded table. Originality remains provisional pending independent literature review.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite enumeration of the first Tribonacci three-pseudoperiod triples could exist.

The finite classification is an effective computable slice of a known decidability problem; its standalone value is the new explicit 55-element complete table and short finite-to-infinite closure proof, not an advance toward a full infinite characterization.
Independent scientific audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The 2022 source explicitly poses characterization of all Tribonacci three-pseudoperiods as Open Problem 30 and gives only the first example (4,6,7). The first complete census at a nontrivial natural substitution cutoff |tau^6(0)|=44 certifies 55 triples, 54 not stated in that paper, and rules out the other 13,189, with a very short finite-to-infinite language certificate. This provides concrete exact initial data and reliable tests for any future automaton or symbolic classification, despite not solving the unbounded problem.
